title: SF353 (2023-2024 Regular): Possessions of dangerous weapons in the capitol complex prohibition

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2023-01-13; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/SF/353/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, as filed (2023-01-13); official copy from revisor.mn.gov. No passage vote recorded. The bill strikes the commissioner-of-public-safety notice and consent language and the permit-holder exclusion from the definition of carry (clause 3). Section 1 is as amended; it is the law as the bill would make it.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1g): (a) A person who commits either of the following acts is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1g): (2) possesses a dangerous weapon, ammunition, or explosives in any state building within the Capitol Area described in chapter 15B, other than the National Guard Armory.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1g): (2) persons who carry pistols according to the terms of a permit issued under section 624.714 in a courthouse complex and who so notify the sheriff;
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1g): (c) Unless a person is otherwise prohibited or restricted by other law to possess a firearm, the prohibition in paragraph (a), clause (2), does not apply to persons authorized to carry a pistol under section 624.714, while the person is: (1) in a motor vehicle, or (2) outside of a motor vehicle to directly place a firearm in, or retrieve it from, the trunk or rear area of the vehicle.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7181, subd. 1): (3) the carrying of an antique firearm as a curiosity or for its historical significance or value; or (4) the transporting of a BB gun, rifle, or shotgun in compliance with section 97B.045.
